Anova#@param fit.en: A fit from {@link lm} with a formula.

Anova#summary.en:
Type II or type III tests of the terms of a linear model. Equivalent to `car::Anova()` in R. As
`car::Anova(fit, type = 2)` or `type = 3` for an `lm` fit: columns `Sum Sq`, `Df`, `F value`, `Pr(>F)`; rows the terms (type III: `(Intercept)` first when the
model has one) and `Residuals`.

Type II tests each term after all the others except the terms that contain it (car's marginality; it does not
depend on the contrasts). Type III tests each column set of the model's own matrix after all the other columns, so
it depends on the contrasts (`contr.sum` is the usual choice).

Errors as car: `residual df = 0`, `residual sum of squares is 0 (within rounding error)`, and for type III `there
are aliased coefficients in the model`. Type II of a model with only an intercept gives the type III table with a
warning.

AnovaOptions.type#summary.en: The type of the tests: 2 (default, as car) or 3; `"II"` and `"III"` are accepted too.

AnovaTable#summary.en: An analysis of variance table, in the form of R's printed table.

AnovaTable.colNames#summary.en: R's column names, such as `"Df"`, `"Sum Sq"`, `"Mean Sq"`, `"F value"`, `"Pr(>F)"`.

AnovaTable.rowNames#summary.en: Row names (term labels and `"Residuals"`, or `"1"`, `"2"`, ... for a comparison).

AnovaTable.table#summary.en: One array per row; NaN where R prints nothing or NA.

AovEzEffectSize#summary.en: An effect size of {@link aovEz}: generalized (`"ges"`) or partial (`"pes"`) eta squared.

AovEzOptions.correction#summary.en: Sphericity correction of the anova table: `"GG"` (default), `"HF"` or `"none"`.

AovEzOptions.observed#summary.en: Observed (not manipulated) factors, for the generalized eta squared.

AovEzOptions.type#summary.en: Type of the sums of squares: 3 (default) or 2.

AovEzResult.corrections#summary.en: Greenhouse-Geisser and Huynh-Feldt corrections of the rows with more than one within-subject df.

AovEzResult.sphericity#summary.en: Mauchly's tests of the same rows.

AovEzResult.univariate#summary.en: car's univariate tests (intercept included); without within-subject factors, car's Anova table.

AovEzResult.warnings#summary.en: afex's and car's warnings (averaged cells, removed subjects, `HF eps > 1 treated as 1`, ...).

AovEzTable.colNames#summary.en: Column names, such as afex's `"num Df"`, `"den Df"`, `"MSE"`, `"F"`, `"ges"`, `"Pr(>F)"`.

AovEzTable.rowNames#summary.en: Row names: the terms (and `"(Intercept)"` in car's tables).

AovEzTable.table#summary.en: One array per row, one value per column.

AovStrataFit#summary.en: Result of {@link aov} with an `Error()` term.

AovStrataFit.multistratum#summary.en: Always true: the fit has error strata (pass it to {@link aovSummary}).

AovStrataFit.rows#summary.en: 0-based indices of the rows of `data` used.

AovStrataFit.strata#summary.en: The tables of the strata, in order (the intercept stratum included when the model has one).

AovStrataFit.warnings#summary.en: R's warnings, such as `Error() model is singular`.

AovStrataSummary#summary.en: Result of {@link aovSummary} for a fit with error strata.

AovStrataSummary.strata#summary.en: The table of each stratum, in order, without the intercept stratum.

AovStrataSummary.warnings#summary.en: The fit's warnings (such as "Error() model is singular"), each once; R gives them when fitting.

AovStratum#summary.en: The table of one error stratum, as `summary(aov(...))` prints it.

AovStratum.colNames#summary.en: R's column names: `"Df"`, `"Sum Sq"`, `"Mean Sq"`, and `"F value"`, `"Pr(>F)"` when there are residuals.

AovStratum.rowNames#summary.en: Row names: the labels of the terms in the stratum, then `"Residuals"` when its df is positive.

AovStratum.table#summary.en: One array per row; NaN where R prints nothing.

ContrastName#summary.en: A contrast of a factor: R's `contr.treatment`, `contr.sum` or `contr.helmert`.

LmFormulaOptions#summary.en: Options of {@link lm} with a formula.

LmFormulaOptions.weights#summary.en: Weights: an array parallel to the rows of `data`, or the name of a numeric column.

LmFormulaResult#summary.en: Result of {@link lm} with a formula: the fit of the model matrix, with the formula's terms.

LmFormulaResult.assign#summary.en: The term of each coefficient (0 for the intercept).

LmFormulaResult.coefNames#summary.en: Names of the coefficients (the model matrix's column names).

LmFormulaResult.effects#summary.en: The effects Q'y of the (weighted) fit, one per row of non-zero weight.

LmFormulaResult.factors#summary.en: R's factors attribute of the terms (one array per variable, one code per term).

LmFormulaResult.nObs#summary.en: Number of rows of non-zero weight.

LmFormulaResult.rows#summary.en: 0-based indices of the rows of `data` used.

LmFormulaResult.rss#summary.en: The weighted residual sum of squares.

LmFormulaResult.variables#summary.en: The variables of the formula, the response first.

LmFormulaResult.warnings#summary.en: R's warnings (from the model matrix and from `summary()`).

LmOptions.intercept#summary.en: Include an intercept (a column of ones before the columns of `x`). Default `true`.

LmOptions.weights#summary.en: Weights for weighted least squares (non-negative; rows of weight 0 are left out of the fit).

LmResult#summary.en: Result of {@link lm}: the fit and the quantities of R's `summary(lm)`.

LmResult.adjRSquared#summary.en: Adjusted R^2; 0 for a model with nothing beyond the intercept, as in R.

LmResult.coefTable#summary.en: The coefficient table of the columns that are not aliased, in their order.

LmResult.coefficients#summary.en: Coefficients (intercept first); NaN for aliased columns.

LmResult.dfResidual#summary.en: Residual degrees of freedom, n - rank (n counts the rows of non-zero weight).

LmResult.fPValue#summary.en: p-value of the overall F test; absent with `fStatistic`.

LmResult.fStatistic#summary.en:
Overall F statistic with its degrees of freedom. Absent (as is `fPValue`) when the model has nothing beyond the
intercept, where R's `summary(lm)` has no `fstatistic`.

LmResult.fStatistic.dendf#summary.en: Denominator degrees of freedom (the residual degrees of freedom).

LmResult.fStatistic.numdf#summary.en: Numerator degrees of freedom (rank minus the intercept).

LmResult.intercept#summary.en: Whether the model has an intercept.

LmResult.qr#summary.en: The QR decomposition of the (weighted) model matrix.

LmResult.rSquared#summary.en: R^2; 0 for a model with nothing beyond the intercept, as in R.

LmResult.rank#summary.en: Numerical rank of the model matrix.

LmResult.residuals#summary.en: Residuals y - fitted (rows with a missing value dropped; rows of weight 0 included).

MauchlyTestOptions.M#summary.en: Formula over `idata` whose model matrix spans the space tested. Default: all k dimensions (the identity).

MauchlyTestOptions.X#summary.en: Formula over `idata` whose space is projected out. Default `"~0"` (nothing).

MauchlyTestOptions.group#summary.en: Between-subjects group labels, parallel to the rows of `y` (the residuals are taken from the group means).

MauchlyTestOptions.idata#summary.en: The within-subject design: a data frame with one row per column of `y`. Default: a column `index` = 1 ... k.

MauchlyTestResult.warnings#summary.en: R's warnings, each once, in R's order (an empty array when there are none).

ModelMatrixOptions.contrasts#summary.en:
A contrast per factor (default `"contr.treatment"`); a boolean variable takes it too. A name that is not a
variable of the formula gives the warning `variable 'B' is absent, its contrast will be ignored`; a numeric
variable (the response too) is an error.

ModelMatrixOptions.levels#summary.en: The order of the levels of a factor (`{ A: ["c", "a", "b"] }`), as `factor(x, levels = ...)` in R.

ModelMatrixResult.assign#summary.en: The term of each column (0 for the intercept, 1 for the first term).

ModelMatrixResult.factors#summary.en: R's factors attribute: one array per variable, one code per term (0 not in it, 1 contrasts, 2 indicators).

ModelMatrixResult.intercept#summary.en: Whether the model has an intercept.

ModelMatrixResult.rows#summary.en: 0-based indices of the rows of the data used (rows with a missing value are dropped).

ModelMatrixResult.termLabels#summary.en: Labels of the terms (variables joined by `:`).

ModelMatrixResult.variables#summary.en: The variables of the formula, the response first.

PredictOptions.interval#summary.en: `"none"` (default), `"confidence"` (for the mean response) or `"prediction"` (for a new observation).

PredictOptions.level#summary.en: Confidence level of the interval. Default `0.95`.

anova#@param fit.en: A fit from {@link lm} (or {@link aov} without `Error()`) with a formula.

anova#@param fits.en: More fits to compare with the first.

anova#summary.en:
Analysis of variance of linear models fitted from a formula. Equivalent to R's `anova()`. With one fit, the table of sequential (type I) sums
of squares, equivalent to R's `anova(fit)`: one row per term (the intercept left out), in the order of the model,
and `Residuals`. With several fits, the comparison of the models in the order given, equivalent to R's
`anova(fit1, fit2, ...)`: columns `Res.Df`, `RSS`, `Df`, `Sum of Sq`, `F`, `Pr(>F)`, the F tests scaled by the
residual mean square of the model with the fewest residual degrees of freedom.

aov(0)#@param x.en: An array of samples (groups), or one sample with group labels `g`.

aov(0)#summary.en:
Analysis of variance. Equivalent to R's `aov()`. From samples, one way: the fit of the model `y ~ g` (as
`aov("y ~ g", data)`), with the values in a column `y` and the groups as a factor `g`; {@link aovSummary} gives the
table of R's `summary(aov(y ~ g))`.

The levels of `g` are the group labels (sorted as R orders factor levels), or the positions of the samples in the
list (from 1) for an array of samples, as in {@link TukeyHSD}. Missing values are left out, and a sample left empty
has no level.

aov(1)#@param data.en: The data frame: an object of columns.

aov(1)#@param formula.en: A formula such as `"y ~ A * B"`.

aov(1)#summary.en:
Analysis of variance from a model formula, as R's `aov(formula, data)` (with `weights` and
`contrasts`): the same fit as {@link lm} with a formula; {@link aovSummary} gives the table of R's
`summary(aov(...))`. With one `Error()` term (`y ~ W + Error(id/W)`) the fit has error strata: the result is an
{@link AovStrataFit} whose tables {@link aovSummary} returns, one per stratum.

aovEz#@param data.en: Long data: one row per observation.

aovEz#summary.en:
Repeated-measures (within-subjects), between-subjects and mixed analysis of variance from long data. Equivalent to
`afex::aov_ez()` in R. As afex's
`aov_ez(id, dv, data, between, within, type, observed, anova_table = list(correction, es))`, it returns afex's
anova table and car's univariate tests, sphericity corrections (Greenhouse-Geisser, Huynh-Feldt) and Mauchly tests.

Between-subjects factors use `contr.sum` and sorted levels; the levels of within-subjects factors are taken in order
of first appearance. Several rows for a subject and a cell are averaged (with afex's warning); subjects that miss
a cell are removed (with a warning).

aovSummary(0)#@param fit.en: A fit from {@link aov} (or {@link lm}) with a formula.

aovSummary(0)#summary.en:
The table of an analysis of variance fitted by {@link aov}. Equivalent to R's `summary()`. As R's
`summary(aov(formula, data))` for a fit without `Error()`: the rows of {@link anova}'s
sequential table, except that without residual degrees of freedom there is no `Residuals` row and no `F value` and
`Pr(>F)` columns. For a fit with an `Error()` term, the tables of the strata (`{ strata: [{ stratum: "Error: id",
colNames, rowNames, table }, ...] }`), without the intercept stratum. As R 4.6, `warnings` has "essentially perfect
fit for ‘1’: summary may be unreliable" where the residual variance of the fit (or of a stratum) is below 1e-30
times the mean square of its fitted values.

aovSummary(1)#@param fit.en: A fit from {@link aov} (or {@link lm}) with a formula.

aovSummary(1)#summary.en:
The table of an analysis of variance fitted by {@link aov}. Equivalent to R's `summary()`. As R's
`summary(aov(formula, data))` for a fit without `Error()`: the rows of {@link anova}'s
sequential table, except that without residual degrees of freedom there is no `Residuals` row and no `F value` and
`Pr(>F)` columns. For a fit with an `Error()` term, the tables of the strata (`{ strata: [{ stratum: "Error: id",
colNames, rowNames, table }, ...] }`), without the intercept stratum. As R 4.6, `warnings` has "essentially perfect
fit for ‘1’: summary may be unreliable" where the residual variance of the fit (or of a stratum) is below 1e-30
times the mean square of its fitted values.

aovSummary(2)#@param fit.en: A fit from {@link aov} (or {@link lm}) with a formula.

aovSummary(2)#summary.en:
The table of an analysis of variance fitted by {@link aov}. Equivalent to R's `summary()`. As R's
`summary(aov(formula, data))` for a fit without `Error()`: the rows of {@link anova}'s
sequential table, except that without residual degrees of freedom there is no `Residuals` row and no `F value` and
`Pr(>F)` columns. For a fit with an `Error()` term, the tables of the strata (`{ strata: [{ stratum: "Error: id",
colNames, rowNames, table }, ...] }`), without the intercept stratum. As R 4.6, `warnings` has "essentially perfect
fit for ‘1’: summary may be unreliable" where the residual variance of the fit (or of a stratum) is below 1e-30
times the mean square of its fitted values.

confint#summary.en:
Confidence intervals for the coefficients of a linear model (NaN for aliased columns), for an `lm` fit.
Equivalent to R's `confint()`.

confint.lower#summary.en: Lower limits, one per coefficient (R's first column, `2.5 %` by default).

confint.upper#summary.en: Upper limits, one per coefficient (R's second column, `97.5 %` by default).

lm(0)#@param data.en: The data frame: an object of columns.

lm(0)#@param formula.en: A formula such as `"y ~ A * B + x"`.

lm(0)#summary.en:
Fit a linear model from a formula. Equivalent to R's `lm(formula, data)`. With `weights` and `contrasts`, and the
quantities of `summary()`.

The model matrix is that of {@link modelMatrix} (but the levels given by `levels` that have no row left are
dropped, as R's `drop.unused.levels`; a boolean column keeps both levels FALSE and TRUE); the fit is that of the matrix form (same pivoting and tolerance), its sums of squares computed
in double-double so that data with a large mean keep their accuracy. Rows with a missing value in a variable of the
formula or in the weights are dropped (`rows` lists those used).

lm(1)#@param x.en: Predictors: a matrix (array of rows, one column per predictor) or a vector (one predictor).

lm(1)#summary.en:
Fit a linear model by least squares, the predictors given as a matrix: R's `lm(y ~ x)` (or `y ~ x - 1` without
intercept, with `weights` for weighted least squares) together with `summary()`. Rows with a missing value in `x`,
`y` or the weights are dropped.

mauchlyTest#@param y.en: One row per subject, one column per measurement.

mauchlyTest#summary.en:
Mauchly's test of sphericity of the measurements of each subject (a row of `y`), on the contrasts spanned by `M`
and orthogonal to `X` (both formulas over `idata`). Equivalent to R's `mauchly.test()`. As R's
`mauchly.test(lm(y ~ 1), X = ~1)` and its variants (`group` for `lm(y ~ group)`, `M`, `X`, `idata`).

modelMatrix#@param data.en: The data frame: an object of columns.

modelMatrix#@param formula.en: A formula such as `"y ~ A * B"`, `"y ~ x + A - 1"` or `"~ A"`.

modelMatrix#summary.en:
The model matrix of a formula on a data frame, with the attributes of R's `terms()`. Equivalent to R's
`model.matrix(formula, data)`. With `contrasts.arg`, together with `attr(terms(formula), ...)`.

Rows with a missing value (`null`, or `NaN` in a numeric column) in any variable of the formula are dropped first.
Strings are factors of the values in the rows kept (sorted by code point), unless `levels` gives the levels, which
are then all kept even without a row (their columns are 0); booleans are factors with always the two levels FALSE
and TRUE; numbers are numeric. The response may be of any type: it only drops its rows with a missing value.

predict#@param newdata.en: New predictor values, with the columns of `x` (no column of ones).

predict#summary.en:
Predictions of a linear model at new values of the predictors, with standard errors and optionally intervals, for
an `lm` fit (`se.fit = TRUE`). Equivalent to R's `predict()`. Aliased columns are left out, as R does.

predict.fit#summary.en: Predicted values, one per row of `newdata`.

predict.lwr#summary.en: Lower limits of the intervals (absent with `interval: "none"`).

predict.nonEstimable#summary.en: 0-based rows of `newdata` whose prediction is not estimable from a rank-deficient fit (R's `attr(, "non-estim")`); present only when there are some.

predict.seFit#summary.en: Standard errors of the predicted means (R's `se.fit`).

predict.upr#summary.en: Upper limits of the intervals (absent with `interval: "none"`).

predict.warnings#summary.en: R's warning for those rows; present only when there are some.
